```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  fig.align = "center",
  fig.width = 8,
  fig.height = 5.5,
  dpi = 96
)
options(elsar.verbose = FALSE)
has_patchwork <- requireNamespace("patchwork", quietly = TRUE)
```

Every map elsar draws shares one cartographic style. It is built from a few
small functions that return ordinary ggplot2 themes, scales and layers, so
you can add them with `+` to any plot, including your own.

| Function | What it adds |
|---|---|
| `elsar_theme_map()`, `elsar_theme()` | Theme for maps / for other charts |
| `scale_fill_elsar_c()`, `scale_fill_elsar_d()` (and `scale_colour_*`) | Colour scales |
| `elsar_palette()`, `elsar_inks()` | The raw colours |
| `elsar_map_context()`, `elsar_map_outline()` | Study area with halo, shadow and neighbours |
| `elsar_map_furniture()` | Scale bar and north arrow |
| `elsar_map_caption()`, `elsar_attribution()` | Attribution caption |
| `elsar_map_locator()`, `elsar_add_locator()` | Inset locator map |

```{r setup}
library(elsar)
library(ggplot2)

boundary_proj <- make_boundary(
  boundary_in = boundary_dat,
  iso3 = "NPL",
  iso3_column = "iso3cd"
)
pus <- make_planning_units(
  boundary_proj = boundary_proj,
  pu_threshold = 8e4,
  limit_to_mainland = FALSE,
  iso3 = "NPL"
)
wad <- get_wad_data()
wad_npl <- make_normalised_raster(raster_in = wad, pus = pus, iso3 = "NPL")
names(wad_npl) <- "wad"
```

## Before and after

The plotting functions use the modern style by default. `style = "classic"`
gives the look of elsar 0.4 and earlier, so existing scripts can keep their
figures unchanged.

```{r classic}
elsar_plot_static_raster(
  wad_npl,
  background = wad,
  legend_title = "WAD",
  style = "classic"
) +
  elsar_plot_optics(include_north_scale = TRUE, style = "classic")
```

The same call in the modern style. The background data recede into light
greys so the country's data carry the page, the box and graticule are kept
but light and labelled in degrees of latitude and longitude (also in elsar's
custom Mollweide projections, where the meridians curve), the legend becomes
a long, thin colourbar (under the title, or on the right of a map that is
taller than wide), and the attribution moves from a boxed label on top of the
data into a quiet caption. `graticule = FALSE` draws the map without the box
and graticule.

Degree labels, 0/1 legends and the caption's "Data:" follow the plot language
set with `options(elsar.language = "es")` (see `?elsar_labels`), e.g.
`79,5°O` in Spanish. On maps you build yourself with `elsar_theme_map()`, sf
labels the graticule in English, since a theme cannot change the axis labels.

```{r modern}
elsar_plot_static_raster(
  wad_npl,
  background = wad,
  boundary = boundary_proj,
  legend_title = "Convergence of pressures (normalised)",
  plot_title = "Land under pressure in Nepal"
) +
  elsar_plot_optics(include_north_scale = TRUE)
```

To use the classic look for a whole session, set an option once:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
options(elsar.plot_style = "classic")
```

## Binned data

Binned (discrete) data get a stepped legend, read left to right like a
colour bar. Passing a `boundary` adds a soft halo and a thin outline.

```{r discrete}
elsar_plot_static_raster(
  wad_npl,
  data_type = "discrete",
  number_categories = 6,
  boundary = boundary_proj,
  legend_title = "Convergence of pressures",
  plot_title = "Pressure classes"
) +
  elsar_map_caption(source = "World Atlas of Desertification")
```

## Building your own maps

The style functions work with any ggplot2 map. Here is an ELSA action map,
using the established ELSA action colours from `elsar_palette("actions")`.

```{r actions, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 6.5}
ex <- elsar_example_results()
actions <- ex$actions
levels(actions) <- data.frame(id = 1:5, action = names(elsar_palette("actions")))

ggplot() +
  elsar_map_context(actions, shadow = TRUE) +
  tidyterra::geom_spatraster(data = actions) +
  scale_fill_elsar_d(palette = "actions", name = NULL, na.translate = FALSE) +
  geom_sf(data = ex$regions, fill = NA, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.5) +
  elsar_map_outline(actions) +
  elsar_map_furniture() +
  coord_sf(datum = NA) +
  labs(
    title = "ELSA action map, Elsaland",
    subtitle = "Where to protect, restore and manage nature for people",
    caption = elsar_attribution(source = "Synthetic example")
  ) +
  elsar_theme_map()
```

An inset locator map shows where the study area is. It needs the
**patchwork** package.

```{r locator, eval = has_patchwork}
npl <- boundary_dat[boundary_dat$iso3cd == "NPL", ]

map <- elsar_plot_static_raster(
  wad_npl,
  boundary = boundary_proj,
  legend_title = "Convergence of pressures",
  plot_title = "Land under pressure in Nepal"
) +
  elsar_map_furniture(north_arrow = FALSE) +
  elsar_map_caption()

elsar_add_locator(map, elsar_map_locator(npl, context = boundary_dat))
```

## Colour

* **Sequential** data use the perceptually uniform viridis family (choose a
  member with `option`, e.g. `"mako"` or `"rocket"`). Rainbow ramps are
  never used.
* **Diverging** data (change, distance from a target) use two hues around a
  neutral grey midpoint: `scale_fill_elsar_c(palette = "diverging", midpoint = 0)`.
* **Categories** use six colour-blind-safe hues
  (`elsar_palette("categorical")`). On a map every category touches every
  other, so keep to four or fewer where you can; fold the rest into "Other".
* **ELSA actions** keep their established colours: Protect `#06C723`,
  Restore `#8803FC`, Manage `#FFEA00`, Urban Greening `#FF0000`.
* **Text** always uses the neutral inks from `elsar_inks()`, never a data
  colour.

```{r palettes, fig.height = 2.6}
pals <- list(
  actions = elsar_palette("actions"),
  categorical = elsar_palette("categorical"),
  sequential = elsar_palette("sequential", n = 9),
  diverging = elsar_palette("diverging", n = 9)
)
swatches <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(pals), function(p) {
  data.frame(palette = p, i = seq_along(pals[[p]]), colour = unname(pals[[p]]))
}))
swatches$palette <- factor(swatches$palette, levels = rev(names(pals)))

ggplot(swatches, aes(i, palette, fill = colour)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 1) +
  scale_fill_identity() +
  elsar_theme(grid = "none") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.title = element_blank(), axis.line = element_blank())
```

## Dark mode

Every style function takes `dark = TRUE`.

```{r dark}
ggplot() +
  elsar_map_context(boundary_proj, dark = TRUE) +
  tidyterra::geom_spatraster(data = wad_npl) +
  scale_fill_elsar_c(option = "mako", name = "Convergence of pressures") +
  elsar_map_outline(boundary_proj, dark = TRUE) +
  elsar_map_furniture(dark = TRUE) +
  coord_sf(datum = NA) +
  labs(title = "Land under pressure in Nepal", caption = elsar_attribution()) +
  elsar_theme_map(dark = TRUE)
```

## Fonts

The themes use the graphics device's default sans-serif font. Pass any
installed family with `base_family`, e.g. `elsar_theme_map(base_family = "Inter")`.
When the **systemfonts** package is installed, an unavailable family falls
back to the default with a warning instead of failing.
